title: Is T the starting point of every ray in the figure?
description: A figure shows point T with one ray going up through A and another going along through N and then B, and a third ray starting at N. Each ray is named with its starting point first, and the first letter of each name is read. A last check finds which names begin at T and which one does not.
teaching_notes: One idea: a ray is named by the point where it starts, followed by another point on it. Watch for students who think that every ray in a figure starts at the same point.

source: Name the rays shown in Fig. 2.5. Is T the starting point of each of these rays?
video_script.why: The child names each ray by its starting point and another point on it, and sees that a ray can start at a point other than T.
video_script.substitution: Read the first letter of every name to find where each ray starts.
video_script.anchor: a figure with point T, a ray going up through A, and a ray going along through N and B, with a third ray starting at N
video_script.payoff_line: No, T is not the starting point of each ray

final_answer.value: Rays TA, TB (also named TN) and NB. No: T is the starting point of TA, TB and TN, but not of NB
final_answer.spoken: the rays are T A, T B, also named T N, and N B. No, T is not the starting point of each ray

never_show: the answer to whether T starts each ray, before the answer beat
maths_rules: The ray going up from T through A is named TA, and it starts at T.
The ray going along from T through N and then B is named TN, and also TB, because N and B lie on it; both names start at T.
The ray that starts at N and goes on through B is named NB, and it starts at N, not at T.
T is the starting point of TA, TB and TN, but not of NB, so the answer to the question is no.
video_script.design: One idea: the first letter of a ray's name is its starting point. The figure stays on the board and each ray lights up as it is named. The method is the same way as the example in the book on naming a ray.
open_questions: The figure is not visible in the extracted text. The worklist lists four rays TA, TB, TN and NB. If N lies on TB, then TN and TB are two names of one ray, which the video says; please confirm against the printed figure.
